problem: The powers of ten have lost their superscripts: "100 × 106 bit/s" and "2 × 106 bit/s" read as 100 × 106 = 10 600 bit/s, which is not 100 Mbit/s and 2 Mbit/s. A student copying this gets a number that is wrong by a factor of a million.
fix: Write "A link at 100 Mbit/s is 100 × 10⁶ bit/s; a stream at 2 Mbit/s is 2 × 10⁶ bit/s, so the units cancel."

problem: "Peer-to-peer lets clients exchange chunks directly, so load rises with users" is misleading: the "so" claims that peer-to-peer causes load to rise, but load rises with users in every model. The real point is that in peer-to-peer the total upload capacity also grows with the number of users, while in client–server it stays fixed.
fix: "Peer-to-peer lets clients exchange chunks directly, so total upload capacity grows as users join, but control and rights management are harder."

problem: The question is worded as "Why can an edge node reduce start-up delay more than it raises average throughput?", which tells the student that an edge node does raise average throughput. The answer says the opposite, that throughput may not improve. The question and its answer do not match.
fix: "Why does an edge node cut start-up delay but not always raise average throughput?"
